Oom Bennie

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Where the clippers hum and the past still cheers — Oom Bennie’s shop is where rugby, memory, and community meet.

Unique Selling Point:
Set in Newlands, on the edge of Sophiatown, Oom Bennie’s tiny two-chair barbershop is a living museum of South African rugby. Every wall — even the ceiling — is covered in Springbok memorabilia collected over decades. It’s a space where nostalgia, sport, and neighbourhood life meet.

Summary:
[OPENING SEQUENCE – ATMOSPHERE]
Soft morning light spills over Newlands. A key turns in a lock. Clippers buzz to life. Rugby crowd sounds faintly echo as the walls come into view.
(Govan VO) Tucked away in Newlands, near the old Sophiatown Police Station — in a part of Johannesburg most of us barely know — is a small corner where history still breathes.
Visuals: The sound of a razor glides. Don’t see Bennie yet, just his hands and extreme closeups…
(Govan link) From the street, it looks more like a corner deli than a barber shop — a faded sign, the hum of clippers mixing with the smell of frying chips from next door. But inside, it’s a tiny shrine to something unexpected: rugby.
Visuals: Wide shot of the shop front — “Oom Bennie’s Haarkapper.” Two chairs. Tight space. Inside, walls exploding with green and gold. We were going to get closeups of razors, scissors, put the barber black bib over the camera… slowmo.
UPSOUND (Bennie chuckling): “Ja, dis ‘n leë muur daar agter — miskien moet ek nog iets daar sit!” (underneath visuals – don’t see Bennie yet)
See Govan walk into the store…Govan takes it in, awe on his face.
UPSOUND (Bennie chuckling, in Afrikaans): “Ja, dis ‘n leë muur daar agter — miskien moet ek nog iets daar sit!”
First time we see Oom Bennie - hero shot – “Oom Bennie on the screen” – with “barber shop graphic look”
Hear rugby sounds under the visuals
Pan across jerseys, caps, match programmes, mud-stained boots. Every wall bursting with colour and memory. Close-up of faded signatures and Ellis Park mud stains.
(Govan link) Step inside Oom Bennie’s Haarkapper, and it’s like walking into a time capsule wrapped in green and gold. Every inch of wall space — even the ceiling — tells a story.
TRANSITIONS: Barbershop sounds (scissors, clippers) serve as transitions — razor wipes to next scene.
ACT 1:
[Govan and Bennie speaking, Govan will sit down with him, he’ll talk to him while getting a cut, but he’ll also talk to him while he has customers. On the background is Danie, whom he plans to leave the shop to]
Visuals: Govan sits in the chair. Danie sweeps in the background. Clippers hum.
GOVAN (Afrikaans): “Bennie, jy het hier begin sny toe rugby nog net op radio was — hoekom het jy nooit opgehou nie?”
BENNIE: “Dis nie net oor hare sny nie, dis oor mense. Dis oor onthou.”
Bennie can introduce - Danie – and Danie can say something about how long he’s been there…
(Govan VO) For more than three decades, Bennie’s stood behind the same chair — scissors in hand — trimming the hair of legends from Francois Pienaar to the late Piet Malan, once South Africa’s oldest living Bok at 96. Pause…Their faces still watch over the walls. Pause
– hear the sounds of rugby from the walls
Bennie’s not just a barber — he’s the keeper of half a century of stories, and I’ve come to hear some.
Govan and Bennie Chat about ONE story on the walls…
TRANSITIONS: Barbershop sounds (scissors, clippers) serve as transitions — razor wipes to next scene.
(Govan VO) Just as Bennie finishes his story, the bell rings — and guess who walks in? Another Springbok. Seems the stories here have a way of showing up in person.
Visuals: Door opens — in walk Jaco Kriel and [second player], smiling.
(Govan VO) Jaco Kriel — the dynamic flanker best known for captaining the Lions, celebrated for his fearless runs and big heart.
Visuals: Close-up: Govan standing, Bennie trimming shaving Jaco beard. The camera catches their reflection in the mirror.
Govan, Jaco and Bennie chat
JACO (laughing): “Bennie, jy’t seker al elke Lions game gesien van die begin af, né?”
BENNIE (grinning): “Ek het nog nooit ’n seisoen gemis nie! Elke jaar koop ek my kaartjies — dis my kerk, daai stadion!”
JACO: “Dis ongelooflik, Bennie. Jy’s meer getrou as sommige van ons wat daar gespeel het!”
VO (Govan): Bennie’s been a Lions supporter longer than most players have been alive — never missing a season, still buying his own tickets, still shouting from the stands.
Upsound: They talk about something on the walls – item two
(Govan VO) These days, Kriel’s passing on his experience to young players in Gauteng — but today, it’s his turn to get a little advice from Oom Bennie.
Upsound: Oom Bennie advice to Jaco…
…then Kriel leaves through the door…
(Govan VO) Another happy customer.
ACT 2:
[OUTDOOR WALKABOUT – THE COMMUNITY]
Visuals: Bennie and Govan walk through the streets of Newlands. Bennie waves at neighbours, stops at a small soup kitchen. Slow-motion: him ladling soup, greeting locals.
Upsound: Bennie: I’ve been in this neighbourhood for 61 years!
Govan: Wow that’s a long time…
Bennie: I turn 80 next week.
Govan Link: In a neighbourhood that’s slowly changing, Oom Bennie’s barbershop feels like one of the last constants. For many here, it’s more than a place for a haircut — it’s where you’re known, heard, and remembered. And when Bennie finally hangs up his scissors, it’s hard to imagine what will fill that space.
(Govan VO) But there’s more to this story than rugby. Every lunch break, Bennie walks down the road to a small soup kitchen — one he helps keep running, just as he’s kept this community fed with kindness for decades.
Speaks to Govan while they are walking, shots of them walking
Upsounds of Bennie and kids at soup kitchen – we are gaining permission for this
Transition back to the shop: see them walk back in… VO Transition line to come after soup kitchen.
(Govan Link) These walls aren’t just decoration — they’re donations. Most of these pieces were given to Bennie over the years… some by players themselves, others by families after loved ones passed on. Every jersey, every photo, carries a memory someone wanted to keep alive — and Bennie’s shop became the place to do it.
Upsounds
(Govan VO) He’s seen South Africa lift four Rugby World Cups — and his walls tell every chapter. Just in time to meet some of the objects on the walls is another former Springbok Willem Alberts.
Willem: Hi Oom!
(Govan VO) The powerhouse they nickname ‘The Bone Collector’ for his bone-crunching tackles. The loose forward is now focused on family and guiding the next generation.
We’ll pick a story from Bennie and talk about Third Item with Alberts and Govan
Govan, Willem and Bennie chat
Bennie: “Julle sien, ek sê altyd — die beste hare kom van die sterkste koppe!”
(Govan VO) And of course, no visit’s complete without a bit of Oom Bennie wisdom…
Bennie Gives Willem Advice…building to a conclusion with this…
ACT 3:
(Govan VO) In a world where everything changes so fast, his shop stands still — steady as his hand.
Do we break the third wall and have the camera man put down their camera and then come tell the story?
Visuals: Kobus sets down the camera and sits in the second chair.
(KOBUS) I’ve been coming here for years — it’s not just a cut, it’s a catch-up. You walk out smelling like Brylcreem and nostalgia.
(Govan VO) Even our cameraman, Kobus Zietsman, drives from Northcliff just for this. Because Bennie doesn’t just cut hair — he keeps history alive.
Kobus gets his advice
Visuals: Back in the shop. The day fades. Clippers quiet. Sunlight hits the framed jerseys.
Bennie sweeps up hair from the floor — slow motion.
BENNIE (final line, Afrikaans): “Jy sien, elke hare het ‘n storie. Jy moet net luister.”
(Govan VO) It was time for me to leave with more than just a fresh cut. I need some trademark advice…
Govan gets his advice
(Govan Link) Here in this little barbershop in Newlands, the stories don’t just get told — they stay. Maybe that’s the magic of a barber: they listen, they remember, and somehow, they keep a community stitched together.
Visuals: Bennie sweeps up hair from the floor. Govan watches quietly.
BENNIE (Afrikaans, soft): “Ek gaan dit eendag vir Danie los. Hy werk nou al lank saam met my… Ek het nie meer ’n seun nie.”
Danie: upsound
Govan: For me, it started as a story about a barber — but it became a lesson about legacy.
(Govan VO) Change comes for every community, and one day these clippers will fall silent. But what Bennie built — the kindness, the connection — will echo long after the last haircut. That’s why he’s passing it on to Danie — to keep the chair, and the stories, alive.
Bennie and Danie: Closes up the shop and leaves



Further information:
Transitions
Kobus (who will be editing) and I discussed using short three-cut transitions with the sound of clippers or scissors underneath to carry the rhythm between scenes.
Sound Design
Sound will be critical for this story. I’d like to layer in subtle rugby audio — as if it’s echoing from the walls — during key moments. We may need visuals or short inserts from SuperSport to enhance those sequences. Expect plenty of buzz and texture in the sound mix.

Story Elements
Oom Bennie’s Advice: Every character receives a moment of Bennie’s wisdom, culminating in Govan’s closing reflection about how barbers listen as much as they cut.
The Walls: We’ll focus on three or four meaningful stories behind the memorabilia — quality over quantity — and reveal how these items found their way into the shop.
Legacy and Community: Bennie turns 80 on 11 November. His son has passed away, so the shop will eventually go to Danie (his assistant). This thread explores the tension between nostalgia, survival, and legacy in Newlands.
Structure
Act 1: Govan and Bennie open the story. Jaco Kriel joins — he talks about mentoring kids and public speaking, mirroring Bennie’s role in the community. The act closes with their walk to the feeding scheme.
Act 2: Back in the shop, we explore the origin of the memorabilia. Willem Alberts appears to share his reflections on rugby history and the artefacts on Bennie’s walls.
Act 3: Kobus breaks the fourth wall, setting down the camera for his own haircut. The piece ends with Govan’s final conversation, Bennie’s advice, and the reveal that the shop’s future lies with Danie.

Extra Budget Items:
Costs / Logistics
Ethically, I think we should cover the haircut costs at Oom Bennie’s (approx. R1 000). Bennie will continue serving walk-in clients, assisted by his shop hand, Danie, who will handle most of the customer cuts on the filming day so we can have Bennie to ourselves. Confirmed participants include two rugby players, Govan, and Kobus — all of whom will appear on camera for haircuts.
We’re waiting on final permission for the nearby feeding-scheme as well.

Script:


OOM BENNIE’S BARBERSHOP — WHERE RUGBY LIVES ON THE WALLS: Where the clippers hum and the past still cheers — Oom Bennie’s shop is where rugby, memory, and community meet
[OPENING SEQUENCE – ATMOSPHERE]
Visuals: Pan across jerseys, caps, match programmes, mud-stained boots. Every wall bursting with colour and memory... AUDIO: Hear rugby sounds under the visuals giving them life
(Govan VO) Sometimes the best stories aren’t played out in stadiums full of fans — they unfold in unexpected places, like this small barbershop in Newlands, Johannesburg.
This one’s about a lifelong rugby fan with clippers, instead of a flag.
(Govan link) Step inside Oom Bennie’s barbershop and it’s like walking into a time capsule wrapped in green and gold.
Visuals: SEE bennie working, but don’t reveal his face yet… extreme close ups and slowmo’s of Bennie’s hands working.
(Bennie subtitles) Can I give you a number three and then I’ll just clean you up?
Visuals: Hero shot of Oom Bennie
ACT 1:
Visuals: Govan Greeting Oom Bennie
(Govan VO) Inside it's less a barber shop more a museum, a shrine to the game that runs in South Africa’s veins.
(Bennie) We try and keep it fun, it's not just about cutting hair, it gives it something extra, and that’s why I created this. It gives a cool atmosphere.
(Govan VO) Many of these prized pieces come from players — others were left to Bennie in wills or passed on by families.
Govan sits down in chair
(Bennie subtitles) I’m not going to cut your hair too short otherwise you’ll look like a worm with a cold.
(Govan subtitles) You have priceless stuff in here.
(Bennie subtitles) I’ve got collectibles money can hardly buy. Look at that ball. It’s made of wood! Three men crafted it by hand.
(Govan VO) For more than sixty years, Bennie Botes has been behind the same chair, cutting the hair of legends like Francois Pienaar and the late Springbok flanker, Piet Malan.
Visual: Bennie still cutting Govan’s hair
(Bennie subtitles) It actually started with a friend, he’s a principal, he said Ben, “Let’s change this white, sterile atmosphere — give it a sports atmosphere.
Comedic music
(Govan VO) Bennie studied for four years to become a hairdresser — mastering old-school tricks, including one that literally uses fire: candle cutting.
(Bennie subtitles) It doesn’t burn all the hair off, just the top layer.
(Bennie subtitles) It seals the hair that I’ve cut, to keep the moisture in. May I burn your hair?
(Govan subtitles) No, not today… (uncertain)
(Bennie subtitles) Are you afraid? Let me show you the flame again.
(Govan VO) Our cameraman then dared me to try it…
(Kobus subtitles) Govan, let him singe your hair a little.
(Govan subtitles) No, no, it's okay, thanks. I can see here it was cut by Uncle Bennie, and this was by the Pakistani’s.
VO: For Bennie, cutting hair is only half the job — the other half is listening.
(Okkie/ Teacher) Everyone who comes here, you hear their problems and what happens in their lives and lend them an ear.
(Bennie subtitles) You know, sometimes I'm even a psychologist.
ACT 2:
Visuals: Bell sound, door opens, Jaco Kriel walks in with a big smile, bennie looks super excited…
(Jaco) HERO SHOT
(Govan VO) One minute it’s business as usual — the next, there’s a flanker in the front row. We asked Former Lions captain and Bok Jaco Kriel to stop by.
(Jaco subtitles) I've never seen anything like this, the ultimate mancave! How long has this taken you?
(Bennie subtitles) Fifty years, if not more. And every day it's growing.
(Govan subtitles) Do you know the story of the Currie Cup?
(Jaco subtitles) I don't know how they made it, but I just drank beer from it!
(Bennie subtitles) See that fireman’s hat? There was a touring team from England, but what are you playing for? So there was a fireman standing there, let me show you, so he took the hat, put it on a stand, turned it upside down. Let’s take the handle off, what do you see now?
(Jaco subtitles) Jissie, how special is that? I think they should tell the players this story. We all play for the cup, but we don’t know the tradition!
(Govan VO) A reminder of how the game’s changed — the old rule books once fit in the palm of a hand.
(Govan subtitles) Oh look at the rules, the old rule book is so thin!
(Jaco subtitles) It would be interesting to compare that old rule book with the new one, there were not a lot of rules back then, that’s why the referees were so good.
(Bennie subtitles) They knew the rules!
(Govan VO) These days, Jaco mentors the next generation of players — but today, it’s old meets new as Bennie shares a bit of wisdom ahead of Jaco’s upcoming wedding.
(Bennie subtitles) It’s a big step, and remember God will bond a marriage.
(Jaco subtitles) Thank you so much!
(Govan VO) [take a selfie] Another memory for the wall!
ACT 3:
See Govan there watching Bennie…
VO: Bennie’s 80 now, and starting to think about who’ll take over the chair — and he’s already picked his man: Danie Pienewald. [Hero shot]
Visuals: See Govan and Danie sit down
(Govan VO) This time, it was my turn to get back at our cameraman…
(Govan subtitles) You know there’s this cameraman from Carte Blanche and I think we need to make his beard wider…
(Danie subtitles) No his wife will klap me…
Visuals: PAN TO CAMERA MAN…now danie does Kobus’ cut…
(Govan subtitles) For the people at home, this is Kobus Zietsman, a camera guy here at Carte Blanche, usually behind the scenes, but he’s the reason why we’re here. He discovered Oom Bennie, and we’re going to see how he keeps his beard in tiptop shape!
(Kobus subtitles) You know what they say about a great beard, with a great beard comes a great responsibility…
(Govan subtitles) Oh I thought it was that with a great beard, comes a great amount of food stuck in it!
(Govan VO) Bennie’s clients are loyal — like Kobus, who’s been coming from Florida for years.
See Govan and bennie looking at beard…
Hero shot
(Govan VO) Former Bok loose forward, Willem Alberts, was another of our invitees. He arrived with a few pieces or rugby history of his own.
Visuals: Willem walks in and bennie hugs him, and he’s brought some memorabilia to add to the walls.
(Govan VO) Among the memories, The Bone Collector points out a cap he once signed.
(Willem subtitles) It’s nice to see those fans that you ran out on the field for, to meet them in real life and see the passion is still there… it warms his heart, makes me proud to have been proud of that…
(Danie subtitles) Daarse! (finished cut)
Visuals: See Govan watching and oom bennie and danie are sweeping away hair and closing up…
(Govan Link) After spending the day here at Bennie’s barber shop ive realised it's not just a place where stories get told, its where your story stays. You come in for the history, and sure you learn about rugby and the community but you leave thinking about the future cos you get a bit of advice from the Oom and you’re looking much better too!
(Govan VO) In Bennie’s careful hands, the game still lives on — it’s a story that reaches beyond the barber’s chair. And as long as there’s a clipper buzzing, his legacy will keep growing with every cut.

Bennie and Danie: Closes up the shop and leaves

(Bennie subtitles) Fifty years, if not more.

(Bennie subtitles) I’ve got collectibles money can hardly buy.

This one’s about a lifelong rugby fan with clippers, instead of a flag. (Govan link) Step inside Oom Bennie’s barbershop and it’s like walking into a time capsule wrapped in green and gold. Visuals: SEE bennie working, but don’t reveal his face yet… extreme close ups and slowmo’s of Bennie’s hands working. (Bennie subtitles) Can I give you a number three and then I’ll just clean you up? Visuals: Hero shot of Oom Bennie ACT 1: Visuals: Govan Greeting Oom Bennie (Govan VO) Inside it's less a barber shop more a museum, a shrine to the game that runs in South Africa’s veins. (Bennie) We try and keep it fun, it's not just about cutting hair, it gives it something extra, and that’s why I created this. It gives a cool atmosphere. (Govan VO) Many of these prized pieces come from players — others were left to Bennie in wills or passed on by families. Govan sits down in chair (Bennie subtitles) I’m not going to cut your hair too short otherwise you’ll look like a worm with a cold. (Govan subtitles) You have priceless stuff in here. (Bennie subtitles) I’ve got collectibles money can hardly buy. Look at that ball. It’s made of wood! Three men crafted it by hand. (Govan VO) For more than sixty years, Bennie Botes has been behind the same chair, cutting the hair of legends like Francois Pienaar and the late Springbok flanker, Piet Malan. Visual: Bennie still cutting Govan’s hair (Bennie subtitles) It actually started with a friend, he’s a principal, he said Ben, “Let’s change this white, sterile atmosphere — give it a sports atmosphere. Comedic music (Govan VO) Bennie studied for four years to become a hairdresser — mastering old-school tricks, including one that literally uses fire: candle cutting. (Bennie subtitles) It doesn’t burn all the hair off, just the top layer. (Bennie subtitles) It seals the hair that I’ve cut, to keep the moisture in. May I burn your hair? (Govan subtitles) No, not today… (uncertain) (Bennie subtitles) Are you afraid? Let me show you the flame again. (Govan VO) Our cameraman then dared me to try it… (Kobus subtitles) Govan, let him singe your hair a little. (Govan subtitles) No, no, it's okay, thanks. I can see here it was cut by Uncle Bennie, and this was by the Pakistani’s. VO: For Bennie, cutting hair is only half the job — the other half is listening. (Okkie/ Teacher) Everyone who comes here, you hear their problems and what happens in their lives and lend them an ear. (Bennie subtitles) You know, sometimes I'm even a psychologist. ACT 2: Visuals: Bell sound, door opens, Jaco Kriel walks in with a big smile, bennie looks super excited… (Jaco) HERO SHOT (Govan VO) One minute it’s business as usual — the next, there’s a flanker in the front row. We asked Former Lions captain and Bok Jaco Kriel to stop by. (Jaco subtitles) I've never seen anything like this, the ultimate mancave! How long has this taken you? (Bennie subtitles) Fifty years, if not more. And every day it's growing. (Govan subtitles) Do you know the story of the Currie Cup? (Jaco subtitles) I don't know how they made it, but I just drank beer from it! (Bennie subtitles) See that fireman’s hat? There was a touring team from England, but what are you playing for? So there was a fireman standing there, let me show you, so he took the hat, put it on a stand, turned it upside down. Let’s take the handle off, what do you see now? (Jaco subtitles) Jissie, how special is that? I think they should tell the players this story. We all play for the cup, but we don’t know the tradition! (Govan VO) A reminder of how the game’s changed — the old rule books once fit in the palm of a hand. (Govan subtitles) Oh look at the rules, the old rule book is so thin! (Jaco subtitles) It would be interesting to compare that old rule book with the new one, there were not a lot of rules back then, that’s why the referees were so good. (Bennie subtitles) They knew the rules! (Govan VO) These days, Jaco mentors the next generation of players — but today, it’s old meets new as Bennie shares a bit of wisdom ahead of Jaco’s upcoming wedding. (Bennie subtitles) It’s a big step, and remember God will bond a marriage. (Jaco subtitles) Thank you so much! (Govan VO) [take a selfie] Another memory for the wall! ACT 3: See Govan there watching Bennie… VO: Bennie’s 80 now, and starting to think about who’ll take over the chair — and he’s already picked his man: Danie Pienewald. [Hero shot] Visuals: See Govan and Danie sit down (Govan VO) This time, it was my turn to get back at our cameraman… (Govan subtitles) You know there’s this cameraman from Carte Blanche and I think we need to make his beard wider… (Danie subtitles) No his wife will klap me… Visuals: PAN TO CAMERA MAN…now danie does Kobus’ cut… (Govan subtitles) For the people at home, this is Kobus Zietsman, a camera guy here at Carte Blanche, usually behind the scenes, but he’s the reason why we’re here. He discovered Oom Bennie, and we’re going to see how he keeps his beard in tiptop shape! (Kobus subtitles) You know what they say about a great beard, with a great beard comes a great responsibility… (Govan subtitles) Oh I thought it was that with a great beard, comes a great amount of food stuck in it! (Govan VO) Bennie’s clients are loyal — like Kobus, who’s been coming from Florida for years. See Govan and bennie looking at beard… Hero shot (Govan VO) Former Bok loose forward, Willem Alberts, was another of our invitees. He arrived with a few pieces or rugby history of his own. Visuals: Willem walks in and bennie hugs him, and he’s brought some memorabilia to add to the walls. (Govan VO) Among the memories, The Bone Collector points out a cap he once signed. (Willem subtitles) It’s nice to see those fans that you ran out on the field for, to meet them in real life and see the passion is still there… it warms his heart, makes me proud to have been proud of that… (Danie subtitles) Daarse! (Govan VO) In Bennie’s careful hands, the game still lives on — it’s a story that reaches beyond the barber’s chair. The Walls: We’ll focus on three or four meaningful stories behind the memorabilia — quality over quantity — and reveal how these items found their way into the shop. Legacy and Community: Bennie turns 80 on 11 November. His son has passed away, so the shop will eventually go to Danie (his assistant). This thread explores the tension between nostalgia, survival, and legacy in Newlands. Structure Act 1: Govan and Bennie open the story. Jaco Kriel joins — he talks about mentoring kids and public speaking, mirroring Bennie’s role in the community. The act closes with their walk to the feeding scheme. Act 2: Back in the shop, we explore the origin of the memorabilia. Willem Alberts appears to share his reflections on rugby history and the artefacts on Bennie’s walls. Act 3: Kobus breaks the fourth wall, setting down the camera for his own haircut. The piece ends with Govan’s final conversation, Bennie’s advice, and the reveal that the shop’s future lies with Danie.

Bennie will continue serving walk-in clients, assisted by his shop hand, Danie, who will handle most of the customer cuts on the filming day so we can have Bennie to ourselves. Confirmed participants include two rugby players, Govan, and Kobus — all of whom will appear on camera for haircuts. We’re waiting on final permission for the nearby feeding-scheme as well.
